about: The providers fxbot's Add provider page offers. Shipped with each release and read hourly from https://fxbot.sh/providers-registry.json. Each entry's fields are described by CatalogEntry in packages/sdk/src/types.ts.

providers.name: Vercel
providers.about: AI Gateway's models, billed to one of your Vercel teams

providers.name: ChatGPT and Codex
providers.about: Your ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu plan
providers.note: Your plan's own usage limits apply, as they do in Codex.

providers.name: Grok
providers.about: Your SuperGrok or X Premium plan
providers.note: Your plan's own usage limits apply.

providers.name: AI Gateway
providers.about: Vercel's gateway to hundreds of models, with one key
steps: Pick the team to bill, then choose Create key.
Copy the key. Vercel shows it only once.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.about: GPT models, from OpenAI's own API
steps: Choose Create new secret key, and give it a name.
Add credit under Billing first, or the key can't run a model.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.about: Claude models, through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible API
steps: Choose Create key, and pick a workspace for it.
Add credit under Billing first.
providers.note: Anthropic says its OpenAI-compatible API is "not considered a long-term or production-ready solution". It has no prompt caching, and returns no thinking. For prompt caching now, add Claude through AI Gateway, with your own Anthropic key there.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.about: Gemini models, with a key from Google AI Studio
steps: Choose Create API key, and pick or make a Google Cloud project.
providers.start: A free tier, with lower limits

providers.name: DeepSeek
providers.about: DeepSeek's own models, from its own API
steps: Choose Create new API key.
Top up your balance first, or the key can't run a model.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.about: Hundreds of models from many labs, with one account
steps: Choose Create API Key. A credit limit on the key is optional.

providers.name: Z.ai
providers.about: GLM models, from Z.ai's own API
steps: Choose Create a new API key.

providers.name: Qwen
providers.about: Qwen models, from Alibaba Cloud Model Studio

fields.name: endpoint
fields.label: Region
fields.hint: A key works only in the region it was made in.

steps: Check the region at the top of the console matches the one you pick here.
Choose Create API Key.

providers.name: Kimi
providers.about: Kimi models, from Moonshot AI's own API

fields.name: host
fields.label: Platform
fields.hint: A key works only on the platform it was made on.

steps: Choose Create API Key.
Add credit first, or the key can't run a model.

providers.name: MiniMax
providers.about: MiniMax models, from MiniMax's own API
steps: Choose Create new secret key.
Add credit first, or the key can't run a model.

providers.name: xAI
providers.about: Grok models, with a key from xAI's console
steps: Choose Create API key. Leave every model and endpoint allowed.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.about: Mistral's models, from La Plateforme
steps: Pick a plan for your workspace, if it has none.
Choose Create new key.

providers.name: Groq
providers.about: Open models, served very fast
steps: Choose Create API Key.

providers.name: Together AI
providers.about: Open models from many labs
steps: Choose Create API Key.
Add credit first, or the key can't run a model.

providers.name: Fireworks AI
providers.about: Open models, served fast
steps: Choose Create API Key.

providers.name: DeepInfra
providers.about: Open models at low prices
steps: Choose New API Key.

providers.name: Cerebras
providers.about: Open models on Cerebras's own chips, served very fast
steps: Open API Keys, and choose Generate API Key.

providers.name: NVIDIA
providers.about: Open models on NVIDIA's own build.nvidia.com
steps: Choose Generate API Key.

providers.name: Hugging Face
providers.about: Open models from many providers, through Hugging Face's router
steps: Choose Create new token, then Fine-grained.
Tick Make calls to Inference Providers, and create the token.

providers.name: Nous Portal
providers.about: Nous Research's gateway to models from many labs
steps: Choose Create API Key.

providers.name: OrcaRouter
providers.about: Models from many labs, with one account
steps: Open API keys in the dashboard, and create one. A credit limit and an expiry are optional.

providers.name: OpenCode Zen
providers.about: Models picked and tested for coding agents
steps: Sign in, and open API Keys.
Choose Create API Key.

providers.name: OpenCode Go
providers.about: OpenCode's subscription for open models
steps: Sign in, and subscribe to Go.
Open API Keys, and choose Create API Key.

providers.name: Vertex AI
providers.about: Gemini and partner models in your Google Cloud project, on what Google now calls Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: global, or a region such as us-central1.

steps: Turn on the Agent Platform API in your project. It was the Vertex AI API.
Make a service account with the Agent Platform User role. It was Vertex AI User.
Open it, then Keys › Add key › Create new key › JSON. Choose the file it downloads here.

providers.name: AWS Bedrock
providers.about: OpenAI's open models, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and more, in your AWS account

fields.name: region
fields.label: Region
fields.hint: Where your models are turned on, such as us-west-2.

steps: Pick the region at the top of the console.
Choose Generate long-term API keys, and pick how long it lasts.
providers.note: AWS recommends long-term keys only for exploring Bedrock. When yours expires, make another and use Replace key. Claude doesn't serve this API on Bedrock, so it isn't listed.

providers.name: Azure OpenAI
providers.about: Your own deployments in Azure OpenAI or Microsoft Foundry

fields.name: resource
fields.label: Resource name
fields.hint: The part before .openai.azure.com in its endpoint.

steps: Open your resource, and copy Key 1 from its keys and endpoint.
Type each deployment's name below, as you named it in Azure.

providers.name: Cloudflare
providers.about: Workers AI's models, on your Cloudflare account

fields.name: account
fields.label: Account ID
fields.hint: On your account's home page, under Account details.

steps: Choose Create Token, then the Workers AI template.
Copy the token. Cloudflare shows it only once.

providers.name: Ollama
providers.about: Open models on this machine
providers.hint: Set Context window to the server's OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, if it runs with a shorter one than the model's.

providers.name: LM Studio
providers.about: Open models on this machine, from LM Studio's app
providers.hint: Start its server in LM Studio's Developer tab first.

providers.name: llama.cpp
providers.about: One model on this machine, from llama-server
providers.hint: Its usual port is 9931. Older builds, and its Docker images, use 8080. Set Context window to its --ctx-size.

providers.name: vLLM
providers.about: Open models on this machine's GPU
providers.hint: Start it with --enable-auto-tool-choice and a --tool-call-parser, so the model can call tools.

providers.name: LiteLLM
providers.about: Your own LiteLLM proxy, in front of any provider
providers.hint: Paste a virtual key, or the proxy's master key.

providers.name: Custom
providers.about: Any server that speaks OpenAI's Chat Completions
